issues.failure_explanation: Pi^S is defined as the L^2 projection of v in V onto S, so it depends on the moments (v,p), p in S. Those moments depend on all DoFs of v, not only on F_1..F_{N_S}; a Lagrange function with index > N_S can have nonzero moments against S. The Remark's alternative definition only equals the L^2 projection when v-Pi v and p lie in the span of the Lagrange functions of the first N_S DoFs, and these are the functions of V^S, which is itself defined through Pi^S. That is circular. The paper also never shows that V^S has dimension N_S with F_1..F_{N_S} unisolvent. The bilinear form (q1,q2) -> (sum_{i<=N_S} F_i(q1) psi_i, q2) on S is not shown to be nondegenerate. The identity Pi^S = Pi_m on V^S, which every interpolation proof uses, is therefore unsupported.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Pi^S via a discrete form with an explicitly chosen SPD matrix G acting on the first N_S DoFs. Prove unisolvence of V^S, and prove that Pi^S coincides with the L^2 projection Pi_m on V^S, for example by a fixed-point or dimension argument.
issues.overall_effect: The central construction (serendipity spaces 'under equivalence of the L^2-serendipity projector') is not shown to be well defined or unisolvent. The interpolation theorems and the stable-projection theorem rely on F_i(I^S v)=F_i(Pi_m I v) and on Lagrange bases of V^S.
issues.title: L^2 serendipity projector asserted to be determined by the first N_S DoFs; well-posedness of V^S and the Gram-matrix equivalence are unsupported (circular)
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new well-posedness lemma and a redefinition of the projector, but the framework and results can plausibly be kept.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated for serendipity interpolants I^{Sf}, I^{Se}, I^{Sn}. The proof only checks integration-by-parts identities between the standard (unreduced) DoFs. The reduced DoFs of each serendipity space are defined through different L^2 projectors (scalar on S=P_m, vector on P^3). Commutation needs the reduced DoFs of grad v (resp. curl v) to match those of the L^2 projection of grad v (resp. curl v). That in turn needs grad Pi^n = Pi^e grad and curl Pi^e = Pi^f curl, which fail for L^2 projections. Example in 1D on [-1,1]: Pi_2(x^3)=3x/5, so (Pi_2 x^3)'=3/5, whereas Pi_1((x^3)')=1. Hence grad V^{Sn} in V^{Se} and curl V^{Se} in V^{Sf}, asserted later, are unsupported. Item [3] is also ill-formed as written, since it takes the curl of a scalar and should read grad I^{Sn} v.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified. At minimum, the reduced DoFs/projectors of the node, edge and face serendipity spaces must be redefined or constrained so the sequence is compatible, and the commuting identities and inclusions must then be proved including the reduced DoFs.
issues.overall_effect: The exact sequence of serendipity spaces is not established. Assertion [2] of the edge theorem and the node theorem both invoke these commuting identities. The claim that the method applies to PDEs involving grad, curl and div through the sequence is unsupported.
issues.title: Commuting diagrams for serendipity interpolants proved only via unreduced DoF identities; reduced DoFs (defined through non-commuting L^2 projectors) ignored; item [3] ill-posed
issues.why_classification: Restoring the exact-sequence property needs a new compatible construction of the spaces and new proofs, not a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis is only v in H^s, so grad v in H^{s-1}, yet the right side uses |grad v|_{s}, which is undefined. Applying the edge theorem to grad v in H^{s-1} (which explains the threshold s>3/2) gives h^{s-1}|grad v|_{s-1}, not h^s|grad v|_s. The stated bound is false at s=m+1. Take m=1 and v=x^2: |grad v|_2=0, but the P_1-reproducing interpolation error in the gradient is nonzero and of order h^m. The claimed rate is one order too high and exceeds the approximation order m of P_m.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the estimate as ||grad(v - I^{Sn} v)|| <~ h^{s-1}|grad v|_{s-1} (or h^{s-1}|v|_s) with matching regularity, and keep the proof via the edge theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimal approximation for the node space is misstated. The proof supports only the rate h^{s-1}|grad v|_{s-1}, and only if the commuting identity (ISSUE-002) holds.
issues.title: Node-space interpolation estimate has the wrong rate/regularity; stated bound is false at s=m+1 and not what the proof yields
issues.why_classification: A local correction of exponent and seminorm matches what the cited argument already gives and preserves the claimed optimality.

issues.failure_explanation: The functions psi_i^l depend on l, yet 'psi_i^infty' is used as if it were a fixed limit in a common space; convergence is never shown. Linear independence of psi_i^l at each finite l does not imply linear independence of the limits, or equivalently that the infinite moment matrix has full row rank. So 'some l makes M^l full row rank' does not follow. The final step uses norm equivalence on a finite-dimensional space, so the constants depend on K, on l and on the polytope shape. Stabilization-free use on a mesh family needs one l and constants uniform in h and over all polytopes allowed by the mesh assumption; this is not proved. The later dimension-count discussion is only heuristic ('most likely enough').

At minimum, a rigorous argument is needed that a single l and shape-uniform, h-independent constants give ||Pi_l v|| ~ ||v|| on V_l^S for all polytopes in the admissible family (e.g. a compactness argument over the admissible polytope class), with a correct treatment of the l-dependence of the basis functions.
issues.overall_effect: The key claim that a computable, stable polynomial projection exists for a stabilization-free method is not established uniformly. The positive definiteness and uniform stability of the equivalent bilinear forms are therefore unsupported.
issues.title: Existence of a stable polynomial projection: invalid limit argument and only polytope-dependent (non-uniform) equivalence constants
issues.why_classification: The central stability guarantee is only asserted per element with non-uniform constants, and proving a uniform version requires new proof architecture.
